survivingClaim: F_q[T] model, exact integers, rule fixed before the runs; no statement about zeta. For squarefree marked rows at N=2 (equal to the completed rows by Lemma P, relative to the model definition), in the window N-lam < d < N+lam with rmax > 3N and sharp degree classes: the probe vector of a quadratic target of prime conductor has row energy 1.19 to 20.6 times the diagonal at q=7 (nine active configurations, r*=6..12) and 2.17 to 18.1 at q=13 (three active configurations, r*=6 and 10). The excess rises in steps (two at q=7, one at q=13) and is not monotone between steps. In inactive classes the same vectors are below the diagonal. Random-phase vectors sit at the diagonal and the aligned vector at operator-norm size in all 30 configurations. The pre-registered rule returns FAILS. The N=3 cube-term observation (target vectors at 2.4 to 5.5 times the diagonal at rmax <= 3N) is measured on 4 configurations with a completion formula untested for twisted vectors; its rule returned UNDECIDED. Reflected dual sums not run. Extrapolation in N and to weighted or excluded-set versions is not tested.
obstruction: F_q[T], q = 7, 13, N = 2 (completed = squarefree rows, Lemma P), window N - lam < d < N + lam, dual length above 3N: the row energy of the probe vector of a quadratic Weil target is 1.19 to 20.6 times the diagonal (q = 7, nine active configurations) and 2.17 to 18.1 (q = 13, three), rising in steps; the pre-registered rule (excess exponent <= 0) returns FAILS. So the diagonal-level (E-K) bound is false in the model in the window, for targets that satisfy the model RH. Limits: N = 2 only; N = 3 cube-term observation on 4 configurations, rule UNDECIDED; reflected dual sums not run; no extrapolation in N or to weighted / excluded-set versions.
